- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.25) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion zones when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment averages 0.3–0.6 over last 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply +1–2% bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to adjust forecast midpoint.
